tagline: Off the Skagit flats and along the shore of Samish Bay.
intro: SR 11 leaves I-5 north of Burlington and runs northwest across farmland at the edge of the Skagit Valley to the head of Samish Bay near Edison and Bow. There it turns north and takes to the shore. It follows the bay around Blanchard Mountain, makes a pair of hairpin turns at Oyster Creek, runs through Larrabee State Park and along Chuckanut Bay, and comes down into Fairhaven on Bellingham Bay.

It began as a logging road in the 1890s, opened as a gravel highway in the spring of 1916 and was paved in 1921. For fifteen years it carried the Pacific Highway itself, until 1931, when the main route moved to an inland bypass by Lake Samish.

moments.title: Edison
moments.text: The village named for the inventor became headquarters in 1897 of the Equality Colony, a socialist commune that farmed and milled timber nearby and folded soon after 1903.

moments.title: Samish Bay
moments.text: Below Blanchard Mountain the road keeps to the bay, where in the 2010s a local artist set a sculpture of the Loch Ness Monster in the water.

moments.title: Larrabee State Park
moments.text: Charles Larrabee offered this waterfront and died before the deal was done, so his wife Frances saw it through, and in 1915 it became Washington's first state park.
